en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ten Ways of Rebirth in the Land of Amitābha Buddha;
the name of the translator is lost; it appears in the Zhou Record.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
There were twenty-two thousand people in all, who were all great arhats renowned to the assemblies;
Mahākāśyapa and Mahā-Aniruddha were among those who served as their leaders.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
all of whom dwelt in the stage of non-retrogression and were adorned with a multitude of immeasurable merits. Among them,
the foremost were the great bodhisattvas such as Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Aparājita Bodhisattva, Nityodyukta Bodhisattva, and Anikṣiptadhura Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Śakra Devānām Indra, Mahābrahmā the Lord of the Sahā World, the Four Great Kings,
and a multitude of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of devaputras headed by these, as well as the asuras and others,
all assembled to hear the Dharma; each bowed at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, since You attained the Way, You have extensively expounded the Mahāyāna sūtras—
the Dharma for the liberation of all sentient beings— and therein You have proclaimed the subtle, most supreme, pure, and adorned Western World of Ultimate Bliss,
as well as the inconceivable merit of the fundamental vows and repeated aspirations of Amitābha Buddha."
"We have attentively heard and faithfully accepted the methods for all sentient beings to be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and shall practice them accordingly.
However, we have not yet heard the method for contemplating the body; what is its nature? We only pray that you will explain it."
The Buddha told Ānanda: "As for the method of contemplating the body, one does not contemplate the east or west, nor the south or north;
one does not contemplate the four intermediate directions or above and below; one does not contemplate empty space; one does not contemplate external conditions, nor internal conditions;

one does not contemplate the physical form of the body, nor its colors, sounds, or images. One contemplates only the absence of conditions (*anālambana*); this is the correct and true method of contemplating the body."
Apart from this contemplation of the body, if one searches thoroughly throughout the ten directions and in every place, there is no other dharma by which one attains liberation.
The Buddha again addressed Ānanda: "Simply contemplate your own body; the power of goodness is natural, right mindfulness is natural, and liberation is natural.
Why is this? It is like a person who, through diligence and a straightforward mind, attains right liberation—such a person [attains it naturally]."
"Liberation arrives of its own accord without being sought. Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if sentient beings in the world possess such right mindfulness and liberation, there should be no hell-beings, hungry ghosts, or animals—no three evil realms at all."
The Buddha told Ānanda: "Why is it that the sentient beings of the world do not attain liberation?

It is because all sentient beings are characterized by much falsehood and little reality, lacking even a single moment of right mindfulness. For this reason, those in the hells are many and those who are liberated are few.
It is like a person who outwardly manifests filial piety toward their own parents and teachers, yet inwardly harbors malice."
"Externally manifesting diligence while internally harboring insincerity—such an evil person, though their retribution has not yet arrived, is not far from the three miserable realms;
lacking right mindfulness, they shall not attain liberation. Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"If this is so, what further roots of goodness should one cultivate to attain right liberation?"
The Buddha told Ānanda: "Listen well now; I shall now explain for you the ten methods of rebirth in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, by which one may attain liberation.
What are these ten? First: Contemplate the body with right mindfulness and always maintain a joyful heart;
by giving food, drink, and clothing to the Buddhas and the Sangha, one will be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha. Second: [The second method...]
1. With right mindfulness, one bestows the sweet and excellent medicine upon a single sick bhikṣu and all those who are reborn in the Land of Amitābha Buddha;
2. With right mindfulness, one does not harm a single living being and maintains compassion for all those who are reborn in the Land of Amitābha Buddha; 3.
With right mindfulness, one purifies the precepts received from the teacher, cultivates wisdom and the holy life (*brahmacarya*), and always maintains a joyful heart.

Fifth, those who rejoice in rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha; sixth, those who with right mindfulness are filial toward their parents and respectful toward their teachers and elders, giving rise to no mind of arrogance, and thereby attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha;

seventh, those who with right mindfulness go to monasteries, show reverence to stupas and temples, and upon hearing the Dharma, understand even a single meaning, and thereby attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
Seventh, with right mindfulness, one who upholds the eight precepts of the fast for a full day and night without breaking even a single one will be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.

Eighth, with right mindfulness, one who can remain secluded from dwellings during the months and days of fasting and constantly attend upon a virtuous teacher will be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
Ninth, with right mindfulness, one who is always able to maintain purity...

If one diligently practices the precepts and meditative concentration, protects the Dharma, and refrains from harsh speech, and if one can practice in this way, one will be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.

Tenth, regarding right mindfulness: if one does not give rise to a mind of slander toward the unsurpassed path, but instead perseveres in maintaining the pure precepts and further teaches those who lack wisdom to disseminate the teachings of this sutra, thereby transforming and guiding immeasurable sentient beings—in this manner [one shall be reborn].
All these people shall attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
At that time, the worlds of the ten directions shook in six ways, and a rain of rare and wondrous flowers fell.
Bodhisattvas from all the Buddha-lands of other quarters gathered for this assembly to listen to the Dharma with a single mind. Within this great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named...

Sāgaramati addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, what marvelous joys and superior matters are there in that land of Amitābha Buddha, such that all sentient beings aspire to be reborn there?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati:
“You should now stand up, join your palms, straighten your body toward the west, and with right mindfulness contemplate the land of Amitābha Buddha, wishing to see Amitābha.”
At that time, the entire great assembly also rose and joined their palms, gazing together at Amitābha Buddha.
Then, Amitābha Buddha manifested great supernormal powers and emitted a vast radiance that illuminated the body of the Bodhisattva Sāgaradharaprajñā.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Sāgaradharaprajñā and the others immediately beheld all the adornments of Amitābha Buddha’s land.
All exquisite things therein are made of the seven treasures: mountains of the seven treasures, stupas of the seven treasures, courtyards of the seven treasures, and pavilions of the seven treasures.
Water-birds, trees, and forests constantly emit the sounds of the Dharma. In that land, the Bodhimanda tree is forty thousand yojanas high;
beneath it is a lion throne five hundred yojanas high, where Amitābha Buddha daily turns the wheel of the Dharma.
The people of that land do not practice external matters, but practice internal matters exclusively;

their mouths speak the words of the Vaipulya, their ears hear the sounds of the Vaipulya, and their minds understand the meaning of the Vaipulya. At that time, the Bodhisattva Sāgarabuddhidhara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we now behold the inconceivable and supreme, wondrous benefits of that land. Now I make this vow..."
"May all sentient beings be reborn there first, and thereafter may we also vow to be born in that land. The Buddha gave them this prediction:
"Through right contemplation and right mindfulness, you shall attain right liberation; all of you shall be born there."
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Ocean-Mountain Wisdom: "If you now wish to deliver all sentient beings, you should receive, uphold, and recite this sutra.

The Buddha told the great assembly: "After my parinirvāṇa, those who receive, uphold, and widely proclaim and disseminate this sutra throughout eighty thousand kalpas will cause all sentient beings to universally hear, know, believe, delight in, and practice it, as well as those who expound it, until the time of the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa."
All who hear this shall attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
If there are such persons as these, from this day forward I shall cause twenty-five bodhisattvas to protect and sustain them, always ensuring they are free from illness and affliction.
Whether humans or non-humans, none shall find an opportunity to harm them; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, day or night, they shall always abide in peace.
Furthermore, Ananda, if there are sentient beings who have deep faith in this sutra, who mindfully recite the name of Amitabha Buddha, and who vow to be reborn in that land,
then Amitabha Buddha in that Land of Ultimate Bliss will immediately dispatch Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva,
Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Dharmeśvara Bodhisattva, Siṃhanāda Bodhisattva, and others.
Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, Bodhisattva Guṇakoṭi, Bodhisattva Ratnakoṭi,
Bodhisattva Suvarṇakoṭi, Bodhisattva Vajra, Bodhisattva Sāgarabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña, Bodhisattva Prabhāpāla-rāja,
Bodhisattva Avataṃsakarāja, Bodhisattva Sarvaratnarāja, Bodhisattva Candraprabharāja, Bodhisattva Sūryaprabharāja, and Bodhisattva Samādhirāja.
The Bodhisattva Sovereign King, the Bodhisattva Great Sovereign King, the Bodhisattva White Elephant King,
the Bodhisattva King of Great Majestic Virtue, and the Bodhisattva Boundless Body— these twenty-five bodhisattvas shall protect the practitioner whether walking,
standing, sitting, or lying down, by day or by night, at all times and in all places, preventing all evils.
Malevolent spirits and evil deities will find an opportunity to exploit them. The Buddha further told Śāṃudradeva:

"This sutra is titled *The Sutra on the Samādhi of Right Mindfulness and Liberation through Beholding the Form Body of Amitābha Buddha*; it is also titled *The Sutra for Sentient Beings with Karmic Connections Who Cross Over the Eight Difficulties of Birth-and-Death and the Flow of Existence*.
If sentient beings uphold it in this manner, yet have not yet attained the conditions for the Buddha-remembrance samādhi,"
This sutra can open the gate of the Great Samādhi for beings; this sutra can close the gates of hell for sentient beings;
this sutra can eliminate harmful human and non-human malevolent spirits for sentient beings, utterly destroying the four directions so that all may be secure and at peace.
The Buddha told Śāgarabuddhidhara: "The meaning of what I have spoken is thus. Śāgarabuddhidhara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now receive this honored sutra upon the crown of my head and dare not harbor any doubt.
However, regarding the sentient beings of the present age and future ages, many will give rise to slander and lack faith in this sutra. What will become of such people hereafter?"
"Why is this? The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Ocean-Mountain Wisdom:

"In the future, in Jambudvīpa, there may be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, or men and women who, upon seeing someone reading or reciting this sutra, become angry with one another and harbor slanderous thoughts because of it."
Because they have slandered the True Dharma, these people, in their present bodies, shall suffer from various grave and evil illnesses: their physical faculties shall be incomplete;

or they shall suffer from deafness, blindness, muteness, dumbness, loss of sexual organs, possession by ghosts and demons, insanity, wind-disorders, cold-disorders, heat-disorders, hemorrhoids, dropsy, or loss of mind.
Such grave and evil illnesses as these shall remain in their bodies life after life, and they shall sit there enduring such suffering.
Lying in bed, they find no peace; their excrement and urine are both obstructed. They seek life but cannot find it, and they seek death but cannot find it.
Or, even reaching death, they fall into hell for eighty thousand kalpas, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.

For hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, they have never heard the names of water or food. After a long time, they may eventually be born among humans, but they become oxen, horses, pigs, or sheep.

Those who kill others will undergo great suffering and affliction; even if they later obtain a human body, they will always be born into lowly and base circumstances for hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, lacking self-mastery and never hearing the names of the Triple Gem. Because they slandered this sutra, they suffer in such a manner.
Therefore, do not speak of this sutra among those without wisdom; rather, bestow it upon those who possess right view and right mindfulness.
It is taught that those who harbor mutual disrespect for this sutra will fall into hell,
while those who treat one another with mutual respect shall attain right liberation and be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha. If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
or sons and daughters of good family who possess correct faith in this sutra and cherish it, they should exhort sentient beings to both preach and listen to it.
All such persons shall be reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.

Therefore, those who have faith and, after my parinirvāṇa, uphold this sutra-dharma—during the periods of the True Dharma, the Semblance Dharma, and the Final Dharma, amidst the turbid and evil world—they shall widely proclaim and disseminate it.
Such persons are truly my disciples; in their present bodies, they shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, the Venerable Ānanda, the great śrāvakas, and all the bhikṣus, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as all the devas,
humans, asuras, and others in the world, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted,
and practiced it accordingly.
Regarding the *Sūtra on the Ten Modes of Rebirth in the Land of Amitābha Buddha* (Shi wangsheng amituofo guo jing),
the "Resolution of Doubts Concerning the Authenticity or Falsity of the Ten Modes of Rebirth Sūtra" states:
"The *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu* [in its] eighteen fascicles places this sūtra in the 'Record of False Works that Confuse the Authentic'."

Question: Since this is not a canonical scripture, why did the patriarchs (Daochuo and Shandao) cite it? Answer: Although it belongs to the category of suspicious or apocryphal texts, its meaning does not contradict the Dharma;
why should its citation as evidence be considered improper? Furthermore, its inclusion in the catalog of apocrypha is biased toward Master Sheng alone;

eminent scholars of antiquity were not necessarily of one mind on this point (as can be seen in the *Guan nian famen ji*, fascicle lower). For example, Tiantai cited the *Fahang jing* (Dharmaguptaka-vinaya-sūtra? and the *Miaoshengding jing* (Sutra of the Wondrous Victorious Samādhi).
The *Fuxingji* (Commentary on the *Sifenlü*), fascicle 6, part 2, states: "According to various catalogs, this sutra (*Faxing jing*) is generally classified as apocryphal;
however, since its textual meaning is correct, it may be a lost translation.

This is also the intention behind the citations by our own school regarding the *Xiangfa jueyi jing*, the *Miaoshengding jing*, and others. For instance, the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, Part II, was originally considered apocryphal."

It was not until the time of the Tang dynasty that the *Dafangguang fo huayan jing shoujie pin* (The Chapter on Receiving the Precepts from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra) was definitively established and entered into the canon of authentic scriptures.

How could it be that because people of that time had not yet reached a decision, one should dismiss it as spurious? The Great Master personally verified its status as being among the earliest translations; it should not be erroneously treated as such. (The above is from the supplementary notes, volume fourteen.
Furthermore, the *An Fashi Erjiao Lun* states: "As for the *Faxing jing*, no one has translated it, though it is included among the doubtful texts."

The *Ke wei shang hong zhi xiang fa jue yi jing* (Sūtra on Resolving Doubts Regarding the Semblance Dharma that Does Not Harm the Great Intent), one fascicle, [and so forth], including the *Miaoshengding jing* (Sūtra of the Sublime Victorious Samādhi) and others, were sometimes classified as doubtful or apocryphal in earlier catalogs.
From the Tang dynasty onward, some were instead published as authentic; these were all matters of personal preference regarding what to exclude or include.
Furthermore, the various masters who compiled catalogs differed from one another in their decisions regarding what to preserve or omit, and all cases are like this.
...and so forth (from the *Ryakushō*).
Written by Gisei Reirei (Inchaku), the ninth incumbent of Ryūgen-ji at Kōrin,
Ōkawa, Bushū, during the first ten days of the ninth month of the eleventh year of Genroku.
